Below is a description of what’s going on and two tiny patches (one for the un-minified grammar, one for the minified) that teach Prism to treat doubled single-quotes (`''`) inside a SQL string as an escape rather than as “end of string”.  Without this, Prism closes your `'select ''hello world'' from a'` literal too early, then thinks the `-- this is a comment` swallows everything that follows.

### What’s happening

1. In SQL, you escape a single-quote by writing it twice:  
   `'this isn''t broken'`  
   Prism’s default SQL grammar only knows about backslash-escapes (`\'`), not about doubled quotes.

2. As a result, in  
   ```sql
   VALUES ('a','select ''hello world'' from a')
   -- this is a comment
   INSERT …
   ```
   Prism sees `'select '` as the end of your string, then the next `'hello world'…` looks like ordinary SQL, the comment line is recognized (correctly) and then—because the open string was never properly closed—it treats the rest of the file as comment.

3. The fix is to allow `''` (two single quotes) in the “string” regexp so it won’t terminate the string in the middle.

---

### Patch for components/prism-sql.js

```javascript
### components/prism-sql.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
    'string' : {
        pattern: /(^|[^@\\])("|\')(?:\\[\s\S]|(?!\2)[^\\])*\2/,
        greedy: true,
        lookbehind: true
    },
=======
    'string' : {
        // allow SQL-style '' escapes inside a '…' or "…" literal
        pattern: /(^|[^@\\])("|\')(?:\\[\s\S]|''|(?!\2)[^\\])*\2/,
        greedy: true,
        lookbehind: true
    },
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```
